characterList.description: A man with a black beard and glasses wearing a black suit, white shirt, and a gray tie, also wearing a gray wig and a bald cap underneath.
characterList.name: Scientist

content_metadata.description: A thorough analysis of a video featuring a scientist testing bottled water quality through pH and TDS/conductivity tests, along with engaging visual elements and intriguing results.

qAndA.answer: He explains that London tap water comes from the Thames River, which is primarily recycled sewage water, raising concerns about potential contaminants.
qAndA.question: Why does the scientist suggest not drinking tap water in London?

qAndA.answer: The pH indicator turns blue or purple when the water is alkaline.
qAndA.question: What color does the pH indicator turn when the water is alkaline?

qAndA.answer: Subway bottled water had the highest TDS level.
qAndA.question: What brand of bottled water has the highest TDS level?

qAndA.answer: He encourages viewers to research water quality further and make informed decisions about their water choices.
qAndA.question: What does the scientist suggest viewers should do after watching the video?

qAndA.answer: He chooses Volvic as his favorite based on both sets of tests.
qAndA.question: What brand of water does the scientist pick as his favorite?

narrativeProgression.description: The scientist greets the viewers and welcomes them to 'Smart Agenda.'
He introduces the topic of the video: checking bottled water.

activities.description: Explains the reason for testing water

characterInteraction.description: The scientist continues to directly address viewers, sharing information and engaging them in the process.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The use of sewer water footage subtly emphasizes potential risks associated with tap water. The black and white footage could symbolize uncertainty and doubt regarding water safety.

keyMoments.changeDescription: A visual transition that heightens the viewer's concern.
The return to color restores the original curious mood.

narrativeProgression.description: He states that he’s been advised not to drink tap water, particularly in London.
He explains that tap water in London comes from the Thames, which is essentially recycled sewage water.
He emphasizes that water has memory and even filtration might not remove everything.
He transitions to the topic of bottled water and starts explaining the pH test.
He introduces the concept of pH and explains that higher pH means more alkaline water.
He links alkaline water to health benefits, mentioning that it can reduce the risk of cancer.

scenes.thematicElements: Water quality and safety, Health implications of drinking different types of water
scenes.title: Reason for Testing and pH Explanation

videoEditingDetails.description: Cut to a stock footage of London
Cut to stock footage of sewer water flowing into a river
Cut to black and white footage
Cut back to the original footage

activities.description: Demonstrates a pH test on different bottled water
Conducts TDS and conductivity tests on different bottled water

characterInteraction.description: The scientist primarily interacts with the props, conducting the experiments. He maintains direct address to the viewers, commenting on the results and guiding them through the process.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The scene subtly highlights the variations in water quality even among bottled brands. The unexpected results, like the high TDS/conductivity levels in the Subway water, emphasize the importance of conducting these tests.

keyMoments.changeDescription: A brief moment that adds a layer of intrigue.

narrativeProgression.description: The scientist begins by testing the pH of each bottled water, adding drops to the cups and observing color changes.
He transitions to the second test, explaining TDS (Total Dissolved Solids) and conductivity.
He starts testing TDS and conductivity for each bottled water brand using a meter.
The scientist analyzes the results, comparing the brands based on their performance in both tests.

scenes.thematicElements: Water quality analysis, Importance of understanding water composition, Scientific testing methods
scenes.title: Conducting the pH and TDS Tests and Analysis

videoEditingDetails.description: Cut to black and white footage

climax.description: The climax occurs where the scientist analyzes the results and reveals the best and worst-performing brands.

storylines.description: Testing the quality of various bottled water brands using two tests: pH and TDS/conductivity.

This was a very tricky and time consuming test to do. Hope it benefits you as it did me. 
I did a pH and purity test of popular brands like Volvic/Evian/Highlands/Subway/KFC/Aldi etc. 

Off course there are other factors involved, this test does not claim to be all encompassing.
